methodological_rigor.justification: Qualitative exploratory study with n=12 semi-structured interviews. Appropriate qualitative content analysis methodology (Kuckartz method) using MAXQDA 24.11. Verbatim transcription and thematic coding conducted. No quantitative statistics applicable. Sample size adequate for qualitative thematic saturation; rigorous qualitative approach appropriate to research question.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Qualitative descriptive study documenting patient experiences of sexuality and body image changes during ovarian cancer treatment. High relevance for patient-centered care quality but limited actionable clinical recommendations. No intervention tested; purely exploratory.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods adequately describe interview procedures, transcription, qualitative analysis approach, and software tools. Appropriate qualitative reporting standards followed. However, no publicly available qualitative data (transcripts appropriately protected for privacy); limited interview guide detail regarding specific probes.

novelty_literature.justification: Study documents well-established gap: sexuality and body image neglected in cancer care. Findings confirm known barriers (time constraints, discomfort discussing sexuality) without proposing novel solutions or frameworks. Descriptive phenomenology without actionable intervention development.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written qualitative narrative with clear thematic structure and participant quotes illustrating experiences. Accessible presentation to both clinical and research audiences. Good balance between data presentation and interpretation.

key_strengths: Rigorous qualitative methodology (thematic content analysis) appropriate to research question
Important understudied topic: patient-centered perspective on sexuality and body image in ovarian cancer
Clear articulation of patient experiences across disease trajectory
key_concerns: Purely descriptive documentation of known gap without proposing novel solutions or care framework
No intervention development or implementation testing; purely exploratory findings
Limited sample size (n=12) appropriate for qualitative saturation but reduces transferability
No actionable clinical recommendations beyond general awareness-raising
chief_reviewer.rationale: Qualitative study documenting ovarian cancer patients' experiences of sexuality and body image changes, confirming known gaps in clinical care. While methodologically sound, lacks novelty and actionable clinical framework. Recommend rejection in favor of intervention development or implementation science studies addressing identified needs.
